findings.issue: `pkill -f "react-router-serve"` matched the agent's own shell command line and SIGTERM'd itself (exit 143); the mistake was made twice, on turn 64 even after being diagnosed on turn 51
findings.suggestion: Kill by PID (`pgrep -f 'react-router-serv[e]'` or a recorded PID), or start each server under a unique port/label so restarts don't need pattern-matching kills

findings.issue: The `meta`-export title bug (200 page rendering 'Not found – Pokédex') was never root-caused; the agent pivoted to React 19 `<title>` elements, which the v8 docs recommend, without confirming what the original failure actually was
findings.suggestion: Before replacing an API, log or print the actual `meta` args once to confirm the diagnosis; the replacement is fine (app/app/root.tsx:50 and each route now render `<title>`), but the unexplained behavior leaves a knowledge gap

findings.issue: Wrote `@types/react@^19.3.1` from memory without checking it exists, failing the install
findings.suggestion: `npm view @types/react version` before writing dependency versions (which it then did, but one turn late)

findings.issue: Ran a Playwright capture script from /tmp where Node can't resolve the repo's installed `@playwright/test`
findings.suggestion: Run scripts that import repo dependencies from inside the repo (it did exactly this on the retry)

findings.issue: Two-three turns spent on shell grep probes that failed (pattern/encoding issues) before switching to a Python tag-stripping extraction for checking SSR HTML
findings.suggestion: Use the text-extraction helper from the first probe; it produced the answer immediately every time it was used

findings.issue: First read the failing build output with `tail` (showing the module list, not the error), requiring a second `head` run
findings.suggestion: Read the head of error output first; the actual message ('Server-only module referenced by client') was visible immediately on the retry

summary: An exemplary run: complete up-front recon, a correct v8 version check against the installed docs, one long design pass, and a first full test run that passed 54/54 with zero fix cycles. Verification went beyond the suite — 18 self-captured screenshots were compared against every design reference, driving three real polish fixes, and the full suite was re-run after the final edit. The only blemishes are minor bash-environment flailing (a twice-made pkill self-kill) and one bug (the meta title) worked around with a better pattern rather than root-caused.

loops.what: Restarting the production server: `pkill -f "react-router-serve"` killed the agent's own shell command (exit 143), leaving the server dead and curl returning 000; the identical pattern was repeated at turn 64 after being diagnosed at turn 51
loops.brokenBy: Abandoning pkill and starting the server fresh with `nohup env PORT=3000 … npm start` (turns 52, 67) and, at the end, killing by PID (turn 71)

loops.what: Shell grep probes against the rendered HTML kept missing expected strings (pattern/encoding issues), suggesting a bug that wasn't there
loops.brokenBy: Switching to a Python tag-stripping text extraction (turns 54–55), which showed the pages were correct all along
